entries.title: Two boys pulled from Venezuela earthquake rubble among 33 people rescued over weekend
entries.snippet: With tens of thousands of people missing, relatives face another night waiting for news of loved ones as the crucial window for locating survivors closes.

entries.title: In Caracas, this feels like the hardest moment in Venezuela's modern history
entries.snippet: Rescue teams are working ceaselessly to reach those trapped under rubble. But as hope fades, anger is growing.

entries.title: Europe's heatwave linked to 1,300 deaths, WHO says, as Germany hits record 41.7C
entries.snippet: WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that Europe is not prepared for high temperatures.

entries.title: Eleven killed after plane carrying skydivers crashes in eastern France
entries.snippet: The pilot and 10 passengers - including five first-time parachutists - died in the incident, local officials said.

entries.title: US and Iran exchange strikes and accuse each other of violating ceasefire
entries.snippet: Iran says it has launched retaliatory attacks at US infrastructure in Kuwait and Bahrain after the US said it hit multiple targets across Iran.

entries.title: Australian man charged with murder after dead girl found in suitcase in Thailand
entries.snippet: The 17-year-old's body was found discarded near a railway track on Saturday, police say.

entries.title: Fourteen killed in Saudi Arabia helicopter crash
entries.snippet: The aircraft belonged to state oil giant Aramco and the cause of the crash is being investigated.

entries.title: Three firefighters die battling huge wildfires on Colorado-Utah border
entries.snippet: A number of blazes have been raging across Utah and Colorado, leading both governors to declare states of emergency.

entries.title: Uganda's leading media outlets shut down by army chief
entries.snippet: NTV and Daily Monitor say their offices in the capital are under "military siege".

entries.title: 117 dead dogs found at California 'no-kill' animal rescue - many with gunshot wounds
entries.snippet: Hundreds more animals are still missing from the California facility as investigators continue excavating the grounds.

entries.title: Australia to double maximum penalty for platforms in breach of social media ban
entries.snippet: Children under the age of 16 have been prevented from 10 key social media platforms in Australia since December 2025.

entries.title: Trump's face is added to select US passports for America's 250th birthday
entries.snippet: The commemorative special edition passports will be available on 6 July, and can only be applied for in person

entries.title: Heatwave breaks records in Germany, Denmark and Czech Republic
entries.snippet: An estimated 150 million people have been experiencing temperatures of over 35C across Europe.

entries.title: Israel strikes southern Lebanon as Hezbollah condemns new deal
entries.snippet: Strikes have killed at least one person, state media say a day after Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement.

entries.title: Budapest's first Pride since Orban left power
entries.snippet: Budapest held its first Pride march since the end of former prime minister Viktor Orban's 16-year government with thousands turning out to celebrate.

entries.title: Why Kim Jong Un never talks about his mother - or her controversial bloodline
entries.snippet: Very few North Koreans know about her, as her origin could threaten the regime’s legitimacy.

entries.title: What news reports from 1600s tell us about life in Mughal India
entries.snippet: Thousands of forgotten news reports are reshaping our understanding of Aurangzeb and the Mughal world.

entries.title: Bad Bunny lights up London with history-making stadium show
entries.snippet: Pride and a party as the Puerto Rican becomes the first Latin artist to headline a UK stadium.

entries.title: Millie Bobby Brown and Louis Partridge on belly laughs, sibling vibes and Enola Holmes
entries.snippet: Brown talks to the BBC about having her "hands and heart" all over the detective adventure series.

entries.title: Sort Your Life Out: The four most common cluttering mistakes and how to fix them
entries.snippet: Tidying expert Dilly Carter shares her best tips on organising your kitchen, lounge and clothes.

entries.title: A 'heat dome' is driving dangerous heat across the U.S. into the July 4 weekend
entries.snippet: Dangerous heat is expected across large swaths of the U.S. this week, according to the National Weather Service.

entries.title: In Venezuela, silence has become a rescue tool
entries.snippet: In Venezuela rescue crews now stop almost everything and ask for silence so they can hear anyone still alive underneath the rubble. NPR's Eyder Peralta reports from the port city of La Guaira.

entries.title: A bridge to Canada may be blocked by the Trump administration
entries.snippet: The Gordie Howe bridge spans the most important border crossing between the U.S. and Canada. President Donald Trump has said he doesn't want it open yet.

entries.title: U.S. and Iran exchange strikes, underscoring the fragility of the ceasefire
entries.snippet: President Trump accused Iran of violating their framework agreement, and Tehran threatened to halt negotiations with the U.S. entirely. Meanwhile, violence continued between Israel and Hezbollah.

entries.title: Trade tensions shake up Brazil's caipirinha spirit
entries.snippet: U.S. tariff pressure is pushing Europe and Brazil closer—opening new global doors for everything from aircraft parts to Brazil's cachaça, the base of the caipirinha.

entries.title: 3 firefighters killed on Colorado-Utah border as wildfires intensify
entries.snippet: The deaths occurred as crews battled multiple fires across a parched region. Two other firefighters were injured.

entries.title: These church members disagree on politics. Together they're wiping out medical debt
entries.snippet: Trinity Moravian Church, a politically diverse congregation in Winston-Salem, N. C., has been raising money to retire medical debt in the surrounding community.

entries.title: Win the family cookout with perfectly cooked hot dogs
entries.snippet: Microwave or air fryer? Grill or slow cooker? An investigation into how to cook hot dogs for the most flavor and the most joy.

entries.title: Tips for taking care of your pets when fireworks are booming
entries.snippet: Communities around the U.S. are putting on epic fireworks shows for America's 250th birthday — but that spells trouble for dogs and cats. Here's a guide to help the animals in your life.

entries.title: July 4th fireworks in Washington: What's different for America's 250th?
entries.snippet: Dozens of technicians will fire off about 851,000 fireworks on July 4, aiming to break a world record in what organizers hope will be the "most memorable display this generation will have ever seen."

entries.title: Heat wave and high humidity will blast much of the eastern U.S. this week, meteorologists say
entries.snippet: Already, parts of the U.S., especially Phoenix and central Texas, and much of the Southwest were experiencing temperatures around 100 degrees on Sunday.

entries.title: Pakistan says it carried out ground operation, strikes along Afghan border, killing 29 militants
entries.snippet: The latest escalation follows months of tit-for-tat military action between the two countries. Hundreds of people have been killed in cross-border fighting since February, when Afghanistan launched retaliatory strikes after Pakistan carried out airstrikes inside Afghan territory.

entries.title: Fact-checking Trump's claims about 401(k) gains during his second term
entries.snippet: Fidelity Investments data shows that during the majority of Trump's second term, average 401(k) account balances have risen by $9,454, or about one-third of the $30,000 figure Trump cited.

entries.title: U.S. Rep. Julia Letlow, endorsed by Trump, wins the GOP primary for Senate in Louisiana
entries.snippet: Letlow, who was endorsed by Trump, defeated state Treasurer John Fleming in the two-candidate runoff after they finished ahead of Cassidy in the GOP primary May 16.

entries.title: Teams scramble to locate survivors 4 days after Venezuela earthquakes
entries.snippet: Acting President Delcy Rodriguez said on Sunday that 33 people had been rescued the day before, although she did not provide an updated death toll.

entries.title: Ukraine's drone set another Russian oil refinery ablaze, as Putin admits fuel shortages
entries.snippet: Ukraine has markedly stepped up its long-range attacks on Russian military industries and energy facilities in recent months, aiming to cut Moscow's revenue for its invasion — now in its fifth year — and make Russians feel the consequences.

entries.title: How the Supreme Court decides its cases — a step‑by‑step guide
entries.snippet: Grasping how the nation's highest court makes policy requires stepping into an exceptionally regulated and sometimes hidden routine.

entries.title: 3 firefighters killed, 2 injured while tackling wildfires on the Colorado-Utah border
entries.snippet: The largest blaze, the Cottonwood Fire, was burning in rugged terrain in southwest Utah. It ballooned Saturday to more than 144 square miles after marching through canyons and mountainsides.

entries.title: The U.S. lags other countries in social media restrictions for kids, but a reform push is growing
entries.snippet: In the U.S., the movement turned a corner with two jury verdicts against Meta and one against Google that galvanized proponents for kids' online safety.

entries.title: France records around 1,000 additional deaths as extreme heat sets European records
entries.snippet: France saw around 1,000 additional deaths last week at the height of its record-smashing heat wave, the country's public health agency said Sunday, as the head of the World Health Organization warned that Europe is now the fastest-warming continent and needs to do more to protect

entries.title: Iran attacks Bahrain and Kuwait following U.S. strikes and threatens to halt talks
entries.snippet: Efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz without Iran's oversight has sparked days of crossfire.

entries.title: Man with same name as U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan is eligible for Alaska's primary ballot, judge rules
entries.snippet: The judge ruled that the division's decision to exclude Dan J. Sullivan because his candidacy was not "in good faith" was not based on the Constitution, Alaska law or the division's own regulations.

entries.title: Trump-backed Julia Letlow faces John Fleming in Louisiana GOP Senate runoff
entries.snippet: U.S. Rep. Julia Letlow, who was endorsed by Trump, and state Treasurer John Fleming are competing in the runoff. The two finished ahead of Sen. Bill Cassidy in the May 16 primary after Trump denounced the two-term senator, who voted to convict him following his 2021 impeachment.

entries.title: Trump says he is nominating former Oklahoma state trooper Lance Schroyer as ICE director
entries.snippet: Schroyer's nomination comes after former ICE director Todd Lyons resigned at the end of May. David Venturella, a former executive at a private prison operator, has been serving as the acting head of the agency.

entries.title: Desperation mounts in Venezuela as the earthquake death toll rises to 1,430
entries.snippet: Venezuela's government said families reported at least 68,900 people missing, three days after the one-two punch of 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes devastated the South American nation.

entries.title: World Cup final day of group play will set the field for the round of 32
entries.snippet: Going into the final day of group play at the World Cup, there are essentially eight teams vying for four spots in the round of 32.

entries.title: U.S. military says it struck multiple targets in Iran as ceasefire is strained by 2nd day of attacks
entries.snippet: The ongoing strikes in the Persian Gulf show the danger of the Iran war again spinning out of control, even after Iran and the U.S. reached an interim deal to try and agree on a final accord to end the conflict.

entries.title: Lebanon's deal with Israel requires Hezbollah to disarm. That might be difficult
entries.snippet: Lebanon and Israel signed the deal in Washington on Friday without Hezbollah. The agreement links Israel's withdrawal from Lebanon to the Iran-backed militant group's disarmament, something Hezbollah rejects.

entries.title: Tens of thousands march in the first Budapest Pride since Viktor Orbán was voted out
entries.snippet: Saturday's Pride march came a little more than a year after Orbán's nationalist-populist government passed legislation and a constitutional amendment to outlaw the event, drawing criticism from human rights groups and politicians across the European Union.

entries.title: At the Great American State Fair, you can find a dinosaur's rib cage. Unity is another matter
entries.snippet: The fair kicked off this week and is a run by Freedom 250, an organization created by President Donald Trump to run his administration's official events.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Will Germany impose an age limit for social media?
entries.snippet: A quarter of German youth spend too much time on social media, with 350,000 considered to have an addiction problem. Education Minister Karin Prien is advocating for a legal minimum age of 13.

entries.title: Germany's development aid strategy under fire
entries.snippet: Days ahead of the launch of the North-South Commission, development aid organizations have urged the German government to reverse billions in cuts to development aid.

entries.title: Pakistan's Geo News apologizes for Muharram broadcast
entries.snippet: The broadcaster Geo News was handed a 15-day suspension for a documentary that was "liable to hurt the religious sentiments of viewers," Pakistan's media watchdog said.

entries.title: Uganda military chief shuts media outlets, slams 'free press'
entries.snippet: Muhoozi Kainerugaba said that he issued the order as he does not "believe in a free press." He is the son of President Yoweri Museveni, who has held his grip on power for decades.

entries.title: Russia's Putin promises security as Ukraine ramps up attacks
entries.snippet: The Russian leader condemned what he called "terrorist attacks on our territory and infrastructure facilities." Ukraine has targeted oil refineries and weapons factories, causing massive disruption in recent weeks.

entries.title: Germany news: New heat record at 41.7 degrees Celsius
entries.snippet: For the third consecutive day, the DWD German Weather Service has reported a record temperature. The worst of the heat is moving east and it should start cooling soon.

entries.title: Saudi Aramco helicopter crashes, all 14 passengers killed
entries.snippet: Saudi Arabian media report that the helicopter crashed in Ras Tanura on the country's eastern coast early on Sunday. It said that all 14 Saudi nationals on board were killed, and the cause of the crash was unclear.

entries.title: France: 11 killed in civilian plane crash
entries.snippet: Police have urged people to "strictly avoid" the area around the airport in Tomblaine. The plane was reportedly carrying skydivers.

entries.title: Fact check: As Europe bakes, should you trust your sunscreen?
entries.snippet: As a heat wave sweeps across Europe, claims are resurfacing online questioning whether sunscreen is safe or linked to skin cancer risk.

entries.title: With 'Operation Purgatory,' Magyar moves to demolish Orban system
entries.snippet: The new Hungarian government is moving swiftly to dismantle the system of former Prime Minister Viktor Orban. The focus: fighting corruption, reforming the media and protecting democracy.

entries.title: New Caledonia heads to polls in vote delayed since 2024
entries.snippet: Security has been high at polling stations as the South Pacific archipelago holds its first provincial elections since 2019. The vote in the French territory was originally set for 2024 but was delayed by violent unrest.

entries.title: Europe heat wave: Over 1,300 excess deaths, WHO says
entries.snippet: The WHO said over 1,300 excess deaths have been recorded in Europe since the record-breaking heat wave started around June 21. Germany logged yet another heat record at 41.7 degrees Celsius.

entries.title: Argentina: Milei's top aide resigns over corruption scandal
entries.snippet: Manuel Adorni is mired in a corruption scandal but has denied wrongdoing. Javier Milei has defended Adorni, saying, "Manuel is innocent."

entries.title: Albania's 'Flamingo Revolution': What's behind the protests?
entries.snippet: For weeks now, images of crowds of Albanians protesting on the streets have been relayed around the world. The protesters say they are fighting for democracy. PM Edi Rama insists the movement is part of a hybrid war.

entries.title: Hungary holds first post-Orban Budapest Pride march
entries.snippet: Tens of thousands packed Budapest's streets despite scorching heat. Former right-wing leader Viktor Orban tried to ban the march last year as part of a wider LGBTQ+ crackdown.

entries.title: Venezuela earthquakes: Nearly 7 million may be impacted — UN
entries.snippet: The projection includes up to two million people in the capital, Caracas. Rescue teams are racing against time to save survivors, three days after the twin quakes that killed 1,450 people. DW has more.

entries.title: Ukraine strikes Russian weapons plant, Moscow fuel hub
entries.snippet: The two attacks, in Volgograd and Vladimir regions, are part of President Zelenskyy's strategy to bring the war to the Russian people and force Putin into peace negotiations.

entries.title: Why is the US targeting Germany's drug industry?
entries.snippet: A new trade probe is reigniting a long-running clash over who should pay for medical innovation. Washington argues Germans benefit from lower prices while US patients shoulder a disproportionate share of the costs.

entries.title: Rome celebrates 80 years of Italy's iconic Vespa scooter
entries.snippet: Thousands of Vespa riders took to Rome's streets to mark Vespa's 80th birthday. The wasp-waisted scooter became a symbol of Italy's rebirth after World War II.
